title: Count the Number of Square-Free Subsets
summary: Given a positive integer array nums, count the number of non-empty subsets where the product of elements is a square-free integer.
statement: Given a positive integer array nums, count the number of non-empty subsets where the product of elements is a square-free integer. A square-free integer is not divisible by any square number other than 1. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Count nonempty index subsets whose product has no squared prime divisor.
Equal values at different indices are distinct choices.
Every value is from one through thirty; return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Represent the ten primes through thirty as bits in a mask.
Discard any value divisible by a prime square; otherwise its mask lists primes used once.
For each value, extend only states whose masks do not overlap, keeping the skip states too.
Disjoint masks are exactly the condition that no prime exponent reaches two, and subtracting the empty state leaves all nonempty square-free subsets.
editorial: Disjoint masks are exactly the condition that no prime exponent reaches two, and subtracting the empty state leaves all nonempty square-free subsets.

tests.explanation: Only subsets [3], [5], and [3,5] have square-free products.
The one-element subset has product one, which is square-free.
